passages.text: At that time some of those present told Jesus about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was present at that time.
Some people were there with Him.
These people spoke to Jesus.
They told Jesus about certain Galileans.
Pilate had killed these Galileans.
Pilate had mixed their blood with their sacrifices.
passages.original: Παρῆσαν δέ τινες ἐν αὐτῷ τῷ καιρῷ ἀπαγγέλλοντες αὐτῷ περὶ τῶν Γαλιλαίων ὧν τὸ αἷμα Πιλᾶτος ἔμιξεν μετὰ τῶν θυσιῶν αὐτῶν

passages.text: To this He replied, “Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they suffered this fate?
passages.sermon:
Jesus replied to the people who spoke to Him.
He spoke about the Galileans.
Pilate had killed these Galileans while they offered sacrifices.
Jesus asked a question.
He said, “Do you think these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans?”
He asked if they suffered this fate because they were more sinful.
Jesus challenged their thinking about sin and suffering.
passages.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Δοκεῖτε ὅτι οἱ Γαλιλαῖοι οὗτοι ἁμαρτωλοὶ παρὰ πάντας τοὺς Γαλιλαίους ἐγένοντο ὅτι ταῦτα πεπόνθασιν

passages.text: No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you too will all perish.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He said, “No, they were not worse sinners than others.
But unless you repent,
you also will perish.”
passages.original: οὐχί λέγω ὑμῖν ἀλλ’ ἐὰν μὴ μετανοῆτε πάντες ὁμοίως ἀπολεῖσθε

passages.text: Or those eighteen who were killed when the tower of Siloam collapsed on them: Do you think that they were more sinful than all the others living in Jerusalem?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He mentioned an event in Jerusalem.
A tower in Siloam fell.
The tower killed eighteen people.
Jesus asked a question about these eighteen people.
He asked if they were more sinful than all the other people living in Jerusalem.
He wanted the people to think about the reason for the tragedy.
He questioned if suffering meant greater sinfulness.
passages.original: ἢ ἐκεῖνοι οἱ δέκα‿ οκτὼ ἐφ’ οὓς ἔπεσεν ὁ πύργος ἐν τῷ Σιλωὰμ καὶ ἀπέκτεινεν αὐτούς δοκεῖτε ὅτι αὐτοὶ ὀφειλέται ἐγένοντο παρὰ πάντας τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τοὺς κατοικοῦντας Ἰερουσαλήμ

passages.text: No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you too will all perish.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He said, “No, I tell you.
But unless you repent,
you also will all perish.”
passages.original: οὐχί λέγω ὑμῖν ἀλλ’ ἐὰν μὴ μετανοῆτε πάντες ὡσαύτως ἀπολεῖσθε

passages.text: Then Jesus told this parable: “A man had a fig tree that was planted in his vineyard. He went to look for fruit on it, but did not find any.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke a parable.
A man owned a vineyard.
He planted a fig tree in his vineyard.
The man went to the fig tree.
He looked for fruit on the fig tree.
He did not find any fruit.
passages.original: Ἔλεγεν δὲ ταύτην τὴν παραβολήν Συκῆν εἶχέν τις πεφυτευμένην ἐν τῷ ἀμπελῶνι αὐτοῦ καὶ ἦλθεν ζητῶν καρπὸν ἐν αὐτῇ καὶ οὐχ εὗρεν

passages.text: So he said to the keeper of the vineyard, ‘Look, for the past three years I have come to search for fruit on this fig tree and haven’t found any. Therefore cut it down! Why should it use up the soil?’
passages.sermon:
Jesus told a parable.
A man owned a vineyard.
He had a fig tree planted in his vineyard.
He spoke to the keeper of the vineyard.
He said, “Look at this fig tree.
For three years, I have come to look for fruit on this tree.
I have not found any fruit.
Cut the tree down.
Why should it use up the soil?”
passages.original: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τὸν ἀμπελουργόν Ἰδοὺ τρία ἔτη ἀφ’ οὗ ἔρχομαι ζητῶν καρπὸν ἐν τῇ συκῇ ταύτῃ καὶ οὐχ εὑρίσκω ἔκκοψον οὖν αὐτήν ἵνα‿ τί καὶ τὴν γῆν καταργεῖ

passages.text: ‘Sir,’ the man replied, ‘leave it alone again this year, until I dig around it and fertilize it.
passages.sermon:
A man owned a vineyard.
He had a fig tree planted in it.
The man found no fruit on the fig tree.
He spoke to the keeper of the vineyard.
The keeper answered the man.
He said, “Sir, leave the fig tree alone this year also.
Let me dig around the tree.
Let me put fertilizer on it.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς λέγει αὐτῷ Κύριε ἄφες αὐτὴν καὶ τοῦτο τὸ ἔτος ἕως ὅτου σκάψω περὶ αὐτὴν καὶ βάλω κόπρια

passages.text: If it bears fruit next year, fine. But if not, you can cut it down.’ ”
passages.sermon: The vineyard keeper spoke about the fig tree.\r\nHe said, "If the tree produces fruit next year, keep it."\r\nIf the tree does not produce fruit, cut it down."
passages.original: κἂν μὲν ποιήσῃ καρπὸν εἰς τὸ μέλλον εἰ δὲ μή¦γε ἐκκόψεις αὐτήν

passages.text: One Sabbath Jesus was teaching in one of the synagogues, and a woman there had been disabled by a spirit for eighteen years. She was hunched over and could not stand up straight.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was teaching in a synagogue on the Sabbath.
A woman was there.
A spirit had disabled her for eighteen years.
She was hunched over.
She could not stand up straight.
passages.original: Ἦν δὲ διδάσκων ἐν μιᾷ τῶν συναγωγῶν ἐν τοῖς σάββασιν καὶ ἰδοὺ γυνὴ πνεῦμα ἔχουσα ἀσθενείας ἔτη δέκα‿ οκτώ καὶ ἦν συνκύπτουσα καὶ μὴ δυναμένη ἀνακύψαι εἰς τὸ παντελές

passages.text: When Jesus saw her, He called her over and said, “Woman, you are set free from your disability.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was teaching in a synagogue on the Sabbath.
He saw a woman there.
This woman had been disabled by a spirit for eighteen years.
She was hunched over.
She could not stand up straight.
Jesus saw her.
He called her over to Him.
He spoke to her.
He said, “Woman, you are set free from your disability.”
passages.original: ἰδὼν δὲ αὐτὴν ὁ Ἰησοῦς προσεφώνησεν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ Γύναι ἀπολέλυσαι τῆς ἀσθενείας σου

passages.text: Then He placed His hands on her, and immediately she straightened up and began to glorify God.
passages.sermon: Jesus placed His hands on the woman.\r\nShe straightened up immediately.\r\nShe glorified God.
passages.original: καὶ ἐπέθηκεν αὐτῇ τὰς χεῖρας καὶ παραχρῆμα ἀνωρθώθη καὶ ἐδόξαζεν τὸν Θεόν

passages.text: But the synagogue leader was indignant that Jesus had healed on the Sabbath. “There are six days for work,” he told the crowd. “So come and be healed on those days and not on the Sabbath.”
passages.sermon:
The synagogue leader felt angry.
He saw that Jesus had healed on the Sabbath.
He spoke to the crowd.
He said, “There are six days for work.
Come and be healed on those days.
Do not come to be healed on the Sabbath.”
passages.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ ἀρχισυνάγωγος ἀγανακτῶν ὅτι τῷ σαββάτῳ ἐθεράπευσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἔλεγεν τῷ ὄχλῳ ὅτι Ἓξ ἡμέραι εἰσὶν ἐν αἷς δεῖ ἐργάζεσθαι ἐν αὐταῖς οὖν ἐρχόμενοι θεραπεύεσθε καὶ μὴ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ σαββάτου

passages.text: “You hypocrites!” the Lord replied. “Does not each of you on the Sabbath untie his ox or donkey from the stall and lead it to water?
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Lord.
Jesus replied to the synagogue leader and the crowd.
Jesus said, “You hypocrites!”
Each of you unties your ox on the Sabbath.
Each of you unties your donkey on the Sabbath.
You take your ox from the stall.
You take your donkey from the stall.
You lead your ox to water.
You lead your donkey to water.
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ Κύριος καὶ εἶπεν Ὑποκριταί ἕκαστος ὑμῶν τῷ σαββάτῳ οὐ λύει τὸν βοῦν αὐτοῦ ἢ τὸν ὄνον ἀπὸ τῆς φάτνης καὶ ἀπαγαγὼν ποτίζει

passages.text: Then should not this daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has kept bound for eighteen long years, be released from her bondage on the Sabbath day?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke about a woman in the synagogue.
She was a daughter of Abraham.
Satan had kept her bound for eighteen years.
She was in bondage for a long time.
Jesus asked if she should be set free on the Sabbath day.
He said she should be released from her bondage on the Sabbath.
passages.original: ταύτην δὲ θυγατέρα Ἀβραὰμ οὖσαν ἣν ἔδησεν ὁ Σατανᾶς ἰδοὺ δέκα καὶ ὀκτὼ ἔτη οὐκ ἔδει λυθῆναι ἀπὸ τοῦ δεσμοῦ τούτου τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ σαββάτου

passages.text: When Jesus said this, all His adversaries were humiliated. And the whole crowd rejoiced at all the glorious things He was doing.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke these words.
His adversaries felt shame.
The whole crowd rejoiced.
They saw all the glorious things Jesus was doing.
passages.original: Καὶ ταῦτα λέγοντος αὐτοῦ κατῃσχύνοντο πάντες οἱ ἀντικείμενοι αὐτῷ καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἔχαιρεν ἐπὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐνδόξοις τοῖς γινομένοις ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Then Jesus asked, “What is the kingdom of God like? To what can I compare it?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus asked a question.
He said, "What is the kingdom of God like?"
He also said, "To what can I compare the kingdom of God?"
passages.original: Ἔλεγεν οὖν Τίνι ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ τίνι ὁμοιώσω αὐτήν

passages.text: It is like a mustard seed that a man tossed into his garden. It grew and became a tree, and the birds of the air nested in its branches.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke about the kingdom of God.
The kingdom of God is like a mustard seed.
A man took a mustard seed.
He threw the seed into his own garden.
The seed grew.
It became a tree.
The birds of the air made their nests in the tree’s branches.
passages.original: ὁμοία ἐστὶν κόκκῳ σινάπεως ὃν λαβὼν ἄνθρωπος ἔβαλεν εἰς κῆπον ἑαυτοῦ καὶ ηὔξησεν καὶ ἐγένετο εἰς δένδρον καὶ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατεσκήνωσεν ἐν τοῖς κλάδοις αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Again He asked, “To what can I compare the kingdom of God?
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke again.\r\nHe asked a question.\r\nHe said, “To what can I compare the kingdom of God?”
passages.original: Καὶ πάλιν εἶπεν Τίνι ὁμοιώσω τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: It is like leaven that a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour, until all of it was leavened.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke about the kingdom of God.
The kingdom of God is powerful and grows in hidden ways.
The kingdom of God is like leaven.
A woman took some leaven.
She mixed the leaven into three measures of flour.
The leaven spread through all the flour.
All the flour became leavened.
passages.original: ὁμοία ἐστὶν ζύμῃ ἣν λαβοῦσα γυνὴ ἔκρυψεν εἰς ἀλεύρου σάτα τρία ἕως οὗ ἐζυμώθη ὅλον

passages.text: Then Jesus traveled throughout the towns and villages, teaching as He made His way toward Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Jesus traveled from place to place.
He went through towns and villages.
He taught the people in these places.
He was on His way to Jerusalem.
passages.original: Καὶ διεπορεύετο κατὰ πόλεις καὶ κώμας διδάσκων καὶ πορείαν ποιούμενος εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα

passages.text: “Lord,” someone asked Him, “will only a few people be saved?” Jesus answered, “Make every effort to enter through the narrow door. For many, I tell you, will try to enter and will not be able.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was traveling to Jerusalem.
He taught in towns and villages.
Someone spoke to Jesus.
This person called Jesus “Lord.”
The person asked Jesus a question.
He said, “Will only a few people be saved?”
Jesus answered the people.
He said, “Make every effort to enter through the narrow door.”
Jesus said, “Many people will try to enter.”
He said, “They will not be able to enter.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δέ τις αὐτῷ Κύριε εἰ ὀλίγοι οἱ σῳζόμενοι Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Ἀγωνίζεσθε εἰσελθεῖν διὰ τῆς στενῆς θύρας ὅτι πολλοί λέγω ὑμῖν ζητήσουσιν εἰσελθεῖν καὶ οὐκ ἰσχύσουσιν

passages.text: After the master of the house gets up and shuts the door, you will stand outside knocking and saying, ‘Lord, open the door for us.’ But he will reply, ‘I do not know where you are from.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people as He traveled toward Jerusalem.
He described a master of the house.
The master gets up.
He shuts the door.
You stand outside.
You knock on the door.
You say, “Lord, open the door for us.”
The master answers you.
He says, “I do not know where you are from.”
passages.original: ἀφ’ οὗ ἂν ἐγερθῇ ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης καὶ ἀποκλείσῃ τὴν θύραν καὶ ἄρξησθε ἔξω ἑστάναι καὶ κρούειν τὴν θύραν λέγοντες Κύριε ἄνοιξον ἡμῖν Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ἐρεῖ ὑμῖν Οὐκ οἶδα ὑμᾶς πόθεν ἐστέ

passages.text: Then you will say, ‘We ate and drank with you, and you taught in our streets.’
passages.sermon:
You will speak to the master of the house.
You will say, “We ate with you.”
You will say, “We drank with you.”
You will say, “You taught in our streets.”
passages.original: Τότε ἄρξεσθε λέγειν Ἐφάγομεν ἐνώπιόν σου καὶ ἐπίομεν καὶ ἐν ταῖς πλατείαις ἡμῶν ἐδίδαξας

passages.text: And he will answer, ‘I tell you, I do not know where you are from. Depart from me, all you evildoers.’
passages.sermon:
The master of the house will answer you.
He will say, “I tell you the truth.
I do not know where you are from.
Go away from me.
All of you do evil.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἐρεῖ Λέγων ὑμῖν Οὐκ οἶδα ὑμᾶς πόθεν ἐστέ ἀπόστητε ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ πάντες ἐργάται ἀδικίας

passages.text: There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but you yourselves are thrown out.
passages.sermon:
There will be weeping.
There will be gnashing of teeth.
You will see Abraham in the kingdom of God.
You will see Isaac in the kingdom of God.
You will see Jacob in the kingdom of God.
You will see all the prophets in the kingdom of God.
You will be thrown out.
passages.original: Ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων ὅταν ὄψησθε Ἀβραὰμ καὶ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ Ἰακὼβ καὶ πάντας τοὺς προφήτας ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ Θεοῦ ὑμᾶς δὲ ἐκβαλλομένους ἔξω

passages.text: People will come from east and west and north and south, and will recline at the table in the kingdom of God.
passages.sermon:
People will come.
They will come from the east.
They will come from the west.
They will come from the north.
They will come from the south.
They will sit at the table.
They will sit in the kingdom of God.
passages.original: καὶ ἥξουσιν ἀπὸ ἀνατολῶν καὶ δυσμῶν καὶ ἀπὸ βορρᾶ καὶ νότου καὶ ἀνακλιθήσονται ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: And indeed, some who are last will be first, and some who are first will be last.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He explained a truth about the kingdom of God.
Some people are last now.
God will make some of these last people first.
Some people are first now.
God will make some of these first people last.
passages.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ εἰσὶν ἔσχατοι οἳ ἔσονται πρῶτοι καὶ εἰσὶν πρῶτοι οἳ ἔσονται ἔσχατοι

passages.text: At that very hour, some Pharisees came to Jesus and told Him, “Leave this place and get away, because Herod wants to kill You.”
passages.sermon:
Some Pharisees came to Jesus at that very hour.
They spoke to Jesus.
They said, “Leave this place.
Go away from here.
Herod wants to kill you.”
passages.original: Ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ προσῆλθάν τινες Φαρισαῖοι λέγοντες αὐτῷ Ἔξελθε καὶ πορεύου ἐντεῦθεν ὅτι Ἡρῴδης θέλει σε ἀποκτεῖναι

passages.text: But Jesus replied, “Go tell that fox, ‘Look, I will keep driving out demons and healing people today and tomorrow, and on the third day I will reach My goal.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees.
He answered their warning about Herod.
He called Herod a fox.
Jesus said, "Go and tell that fox this message."
He said, "Look, I am driving out demons."
He said, "I am healing people."
I will do this today.
I will do this tomorrow.
On the third day, I will finish my work.
I will reach my goal.
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Πορευθέντες εἴπατε τῇ ἀλώπεκι ταύτῃ Ἰδοὺ ἐκβάλλω δαιμόνια καὶ ἰάσεις ἀποτελῶ σήμερον καὶ αὔριον καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ τελειοῦμαι

passages.text: Nevertheless, I must keep going today and tomorrow and the next day, for it is not admissible for a prophet to perish outside of Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees.
Jesus said he must continue his journey.
He said he must go on today.
He said he must go on tomorrow.
He said he must go on the next day.
Jesus explained that a prophet cannot die outside Jerusalem.
He said it is not allowed for a prophet to perish anywhere except Jerusalem.
passages.original: πλὴν δεῖ με σήμερον καὶ αὔριον καὶ τῇ ἐχομένῃ πορεύεσθαι ὅτι οὐκ ἐνδέχεται προφήτην ἀπολέσθαι ἔξω Ἰερουσαλήμ

passages.text: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her, how often I have longed to gather your children together as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling!
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Jerusalem.
Jerusalem is the city that kills the prophets.
Jerusalem stones those whom God sends to her.
Jesus said he often wanted to gather Jerusalem’s children together.
He wanted to gather them as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings.
But the people of Jerusalem were not willing.
passages.original: Ἰερουσαλὴμ Ἰερουσαλήμ ἡ ἀποκτείνουσα τοὺς προφήτας καὶ λιθοβολοῦσα τοὺς ἀπεσταλμένους πρὸς αὐτήν ποσάκις ἠθέλησα ἐπισυνάξαι τὰ τέκνα σου ὃν τρόπον ὄρνις τὴν ἑαυτῆς νοσσιὰν ὑπὸ τὰς πτέρυγας καὶ οὐκ ἠθελήσατε

passages.text: Look, your house is left to you desolate. And I tell you that you will not see Me again until you say, ‘Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.’”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people of Jerusalem.
Jesus said their house would be left empty.
He said their house would be left without protection or blessing.
Jesus told them they would not see Him again.
He said they would not see Him until they said, “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.”
passages.original: ἰδοὺ ἀφίεται ὑμῖν ὁ οἶκος ὑμῶν λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν οὐ μὴ ἴδητέ με ἕως ἥξει ὅτε εἴπητε Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου
